subject.title: Per-agent compaction and contextPruning overrides in agents.list

question: Should OpenClaw support `agents.list[].compaction` and `agents.list[].contextPruning` as a public per-agent config contract, and should https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/88506 be the landing path?
rationale: The source-reproduced gap is real, but the fix adds config surface and changes compaction/provider/session routing semantics, which repository policy treats as maintainer product direction rather than an automatic bug fix.

options.title: Sponsor the additive per-agent contract
options.body: Approve the config direction, require deep-merge semantics with docs/tests/upgrade proof, and use the open PR as the repair or replacement path.

options.title: Narrow to compaction model first
options.body: Accept only `agents.list[].compaction.model` now and defer broader compaction/context-pruning overrides to a later design issue.

options.title: Keep defaults-only behavior
options.body: Decline this config expansion and close or redirect the open implementation attempts, leaving users with global defaults or separate instances.

recommendation.title: Sponsor the additive per-agent contract
recommendation.body: Approve the config direction, require deep-merge semantics with docs/tests/upgrade proof, and use the open PR as the repair or replacement path.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent central schema/config and compaction-helper history makes this the best available owner for deciding the supported contract shape.
